milestones.name: On the Mac, one cooked mesh is culled and drawn a meshlet at a time by the GPU's object and mesh stages, and the picture matches the path it replaces
milestones.quality_bar: A meshlet path as a shipped GPU-driven renderer has one, such as Alan Wake 2's mesh-shader geometry: the player cannot tell it from drawing everything. Held to that literally where it can be: the same bytes with the cull on as with it off, and the frame-contract outputs of the path it replaces.

items.statement: A launch that names `mesh-stages` on this Mac gets a device with the object and mesh stages enabled and the limits the path needs, and the registry reports them. A launch that names nothing gets the device it gets today. An unknown name, and `mesh-stages` on an adapter that does not offer them, are each refused by name before a device is made.
items.ask: Is there one function in the registry that turns a launch's list into the device request, shared with `ray-query`, and does every host that asks go through it?

items.statement: On a cooked mesh that has meshlets facing away, meshlets outside the view and meshlets cut by each frustum plane, the mesh-stage path's submitted bytes with its cull on equal its bytes with the cull off, at every frame of a scripted camera path that turns, passes through the mesh and crosses a cut.
items.ask: Does the proof assert that the cull rejected meshlets for each reason (the cone, each plane) on that path, with a count that is not zero, so the equality is not vacuous? Is the cull's rule one function text compiled into both the compute pass and the object stage?

items.statement: With its cull off, a mesh-stage frame holds what the path it replaces holds in every output the frame contract carries: colour, depth, motion and reactive coverage, lit, shadowed and textured, with history valid and in the first frame after a cut. Each output agrees at a tolerance the test states with its reason, apart from pixels the proof shows lie on a triangle's edge or a depth tie, which it counts. The difference images are retained.
items.ask: Would a mesh stage that wrote a wrong normal, motion delta or history flag across a visible area fail at the stated tolerances? Does the proof show where the pixels it does not judge lie, and not assume it?

items.statement: The frame reports the cooked path that was asked for and the path it resolved to. `Auto` resolves to the path chosen today. An explicit `MeshStages` on a device without the stages is refused by name when the scene is prepared. On the mesh-stage path the forward pass records one mesh draw for each placement, and no cull pass and no indexed indirect draw for it.
items.ask: Is the report the resolved path and not an echo of the request, so that the indirect path cannot pass as the mesh stages?

items.statement: The stage pipelines and the fallback's are created through the device's creation authority before the scene is ready, and the ledger counts them. A stage pipeline that fails to build resolves the scene to the fallback before it is ready, and the report says so. Recording a frame creates no pipeline. A material reload that was asked for still prepares its candidate off the frame.

On a device whose limits cannot bind one mesh's streams as storage, and on one whose limits cannot dispatch its meshlets in one draw, that mesh draws through the fallback and the mesh beside it through the stages, in the same frame, each whole. Nothing of the excluded mesh is bound to a stage pipeline, no validation error is raised, and the report counts the mesh with the limit that excluded it.
items.ask: Is eligibility decided when the mesh is staged, before a buffer is made for it, against the limits of the device generation and not the adapter's?

items.statement: In a scene that draws one mesh through the stages and one through the fallback, an accepted material reload shows on both from the submission it reports as installed. A refused reload leaves both drawing the last accepted material and reports its diagnostics. A frame recorded with the candidate and discarded installs nothing, and the next frame draws the candidate on both. No submitted frame draws the two paths with different materials.
items.ask: Does the proof read the edit from pixels a stage pipeline drew, and not only from the reload's outcome?

items.statement: A scene that did not resolve to the mesh stages uploads no meshlet storage and changes no buffer usage, on a device with the stages as on one without: its resident bytes are those of main. A scene that did holds each eligible mesh's meshlet storage, copied under the upload budget with the mesh and counted in its residency.
No exact baseline moves: with no request, and on the direct and indirect paths, every registered image on the Mac's two recipes and in Chrome is the one on main.

milestones.name: The valley's terrain and cooked meshes draw through the object and mesh stages in the main view and the Sun's shadow maps, through edits and device loss, with the cost of both paths on record
milestones.quality_bar: The valley as a shipped GPU-driven renderer draws it, such as Alan Wake 2's meshlet geometry: no hole, flicker or popping meshlet anywhere on the route, and the shadows the existing path casts. The cost of both paths is on record line by line, as CULLING's paired rows are.

items.statement: In the valley, on the moving route and under snap turns, every cooked placement's mesh-stage bytes with the cull on equal its bytes with the cull off, at every frame.

Each of the Sun's map passes, the two cascades and the top-down height layer, stores through the stages with its cull on the depth it stores with the cull off, to the byte, at noon and at a low Sun. A pass that a mesh only partly reaches launches fewer mesh workgroups than the mesh has meshlets.
items.ask: Does a diagnostic count show meshlets rejected in a shadow pass on the valley, so the equality is not vacuous?

items.statement: With its cull off, each of those three maps holds what the existing caster stores for the same scene: the same texels covered and the same depth, at a tolerance the test states with its reason, apart from texels the proof shows lie on a triangle's edge, which it counts. This holds at noon and at a low Sun over the valley's terrain, where the faces turned from the Sun carry the shadow.
items.ask: Would a caster drawn one-sided, or with another placement's transform, fail this proof at the low Sun?

items.statement: On the mesh-stage path the valley is the valley the existing path draws, at rest and in motion, at noon and at a low Sun: it passes this item's inspection list.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills at the route's stops at noon and at a low Sun and a `realtime` sequence of the route with its snap turns, on the mesh-stage path, with the same stops on the existing path beside them, whole and as native-size crops. The list: (1) terrain is whole to the screen's border and at the near plane, with no meshlet-sized hole; (2) ridge lines and mesh silhouettes are unbroken; (3) every cooked mesh is whole from inside, beside and far away; (4) terrain and meshes cast the shadows they cast on the existing path, with no hole or light leak at a low Sun, near the camera, in the middle distance and beyond the cascades; (5) materials, lighting and texture read as they do at the existing path's stop; (6) in motion nothing pops, flickers or arrives late at the screen's edge, and no cooked surface smears or trails after a snap turn or a cut.

items.statement: An edited cooked mesh switches on the mesh-stage path in the publication's frame, with its placements. No frame draws new meshlet tables against old vertices or old tables against new vertices, and a refused publication changes nothing. An edit that makes a mesh ineligible, or eligible again, moves that mesh alone to the other path in the same frame.
items.ask: Is the switch frame the one the content publication names, from the same run that shows the image change?

items.statement: After a device replacement the path resolves again and draws the bytes it drew before, an accepted material edit draws again on both paths once it has validated there, and a frame that is recorded and discarded leaves the next frame right.

For both paths on the valley's route at 1280×720 and 1920×1080, with the machine's load, the record holds: frame GPU time and frame CPU time as the design defines them; the GPU time of the cull pass, the forward pass and each of the Sun's map passes by name; the draws recorded; the meshlets and the triangles submitted and rejected in each pass, with terrain kept apart from the other cooked meshes; and resident bytes. Each tripwire of the design's cost account that the record trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.
No exact baseline moves: with no request, and on the direct and indirect paths, every registered image on the Mac's two recipes and in Chrome is the one on main.

milestones.name: The record says whether the object and mesh stages measured faster on this Mac, and the Mac window uses them by default only where they did
milestones.quality_bar: A promotion record a reader can trust, as APPLE-TILE's integrated record is: paired, taken in one quiet sitting, its conclusion recomputable from its rows, and nothing claimed for a Mac, a recipe or a shadow method that was not run.

items.statement: The design's eight runs are retained from one sitting with other builders paused: the valley's route on this Mac on the Apple tile recipe, with capture off and the Sun's shadows as maps, at 1280×720 and 1920×1080, the existing path and the mesh stages each run twice, interleaved. For every frame of every run the record holds frame GPU time and frame CPU time. For every run it holds their medians, M2.7's other rows, the load and the thermal state. No figure in the record decides this item.
items.ask: Was the record taken in one sitting with other builders paused, on the final build, in the design's order, and do the retained frames give the medians it states?

items.statement: The record states, for each figure at each extent, the spread and whether the mesh stages were no higher, lower or higher, and its conclusion: promoted, no measurable effect or slower. That conclusion is what the design's rule gives from the retained frames, and the registry's qualified list holds this Mac's entry exactly when the conclusion is promoted.
items.ask: Is the rule the script applies the design's, figure for figure, and does the list in the code match the conclusion?

items.statement: With a qualified entry present, an ordinary launch of the Mac window asks for `mesh-stages`, and `Auto` draws through the stages, only when the adapter is the entry's and offers the stages, the recipe is Apple tile and the Sun's shadows are maps. Outside any one of those the launch makes the device it makes today and draws the existing path, and nothing is refused. A launch that names `mesh-stages` on an adapter without them is still refused by name. A capture or a test asks only for what it names. All of this holds with the list empty too.
items.ask: Is an ordinary launch on this Mac exercised through the host on both recipes, with the cases this Mac cannot show (another adapter, the stages not offered) exercised through the registry's function? Is the Sun shadow method that `Auto` reads the scene's resolved one wherever `RAY-TRACING` has added it?

items.statement: If the record promotes the path, an ordinary launch of the Mac window on this Mac reports the mesh stages, and the valley it shows passes M2.4's inspection list on the final build. If it does not, an ordinary launch reports the existing path and nothing more is inspected.
items.inspect: If promoted: one capture pass of an ordinary launch on the final build, `fixed` stills at the route's stops at noon and at a low Sun and a `realtime` sequence of the route, judged by M2.4's list. If not: the ordinary launch's report.

items.statement: The record says, from its rows, what share of cooked triangles the cone test and the frustum test each removed in each pass, for terrain and for the other cooked meshes apart, and what the paired times say the path saved. From the share measured on the other cooked meshes it says what the same tests would be expected to remove from the exit scene's entities, so that the next plan can decide whether entities are drawn this way.
items.ask: Is the expectation for entities derived from triangle shares measured on meshes like the exit scene's props, with its assumptions stated, and not asserted?

items.statement: A creator can select the path for a scene from the public documentation: the launch request, the scene's request, what it resolves to on a device without the stages and for a mesh the device cannot bind, when the Mac window selects it unasked, and what was measured.
items.ask: Could an agent that has read only the public documentation launch a scene on the mesh stages on this Mac and read back that it did?

items.statement: The maturity ledger has a row for the mesh-stage path, with implementation, correctness, visuals and device kept apart, and claims nothing for a Mac, a recipe or a target that was not run.
items.ask: Does the row match what M1 to M3 ran, with the physical iPhone recorded as owed?

items.statement: Every exact baseline holds after promotion, because the verifier's runs name no hardware feature.
